pomodoros.subject: Writing: summarise, then pick a side

content.content: Read every sentence ALOUD. A summary keeps the big idea in your own words and leaves out small details and your opinion. A main idea sentence must PICK A SIDE: it names the choice you support and gives the reason in the same sentence. “Both are good” does not pick a side.

Practice passages (invented for this exercise; the numbers are NOT from real studies). Should a Doha neighbourhood spend its money on shade trees or on air-conditioned bus shelters?

Passage A. Planting 20 shade trees along a bus route cost QAR 12,000 in total, and measurements under the trees showed a street temperature 4 degrees lower than in the sun. The trees need watering every day for the first two years.

Passage B. One air-conditioned bus shelter costs QAR 90,000 and keeps waiting riders at 24 degrees, even in August. It uses electricity all day, so the yearly power bill is QAR 7,000.

content.question: Which is the best SUMMARY of Passage A?
choices: B) Shade trees are a low-cost way to cool a bus route, but they need daily watering at first.
C) Trees are better than shelters.

content.question: Summarise Passage B in ONE sentence of your own words (no opinion).
Which is a main idea sentence that PICKS A SIDE?
choices: A) Shade trees and shelters are both options.
B) Because trees cost far less, Doha should plant shade trees on bus routes first.
C) This passage is about trees.

content.question: Write YOUR main idea sentence. It must pick a side. Start with: Doha should … or Because …
Write ONE paragraph (5 to 6 sentences). Sentence 1 = your main idea sentence. Then: Evidence (quote ONE number from a passage), Explain, Explain again or Counter, and Link. Read it aloud.
Type the number you quoted and say which passage it came from.
Repair this fragment: Which cost far less than a shelter.
Fix the punctuation and rewrite: Because trees need water, The city must plan carefully.
How many fragments did you find and fix when you read your paragraph aloud?

pomodoros.subject: Math: the Pythagorean theorem, all the way

content.content: Right triangle: a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse (longest side, opposite the right angle). To find c: add the squares, THEN take the square root (√). The sum is NOT the answer. To find a leg: c² − a², THEN square root. The hypotenuse must be the longest side. Squares to know: 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, 169, 196, 225, 256, 289, 625.

content.question: A right triangle has legs of 6 m and 8 m. Find the hypotenuse.
A right triangle has legs of 5 m and 12 m. Find the hypotenuse.
Steps for Questions 1 and 2: write a² + b² = c², the numbers, the sum, then the square root with the unit.
A 13 ft ladder leans on a wall. The foot of the ladder is 5 ft from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
A rectangular screen is 24 cm wide and 7 cm tall. How long is its diagonal?
Steps for Question 4: say which side is unknown, then show c² − a² and the square root.

content.content:
A student asks: does the amount of water change how tall bean plants grow? She sets up four groups of 10 plants. The groups get 0, 50, 100 and 200 mL of water a day. All plants have the same soil, light and pot size. After 14 days she measures the average height of each group.
Water per day (mL)050100200
Average height (cm)5101515
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.

content.question: What is the independent variable (the one thing she changes on purpose)?
What is the dependent variable (what she measures)?
Which things must be kept the SAME so the test is fair?
choices: B) Soil, light and pot size

content.question: Why does she use 10 plants in each group?
choices: A) So one unusual plant does not decide the result
B) Because 10 is a lucky number
D) So the plants can talk

content.question: By what percent did the average height increase from the 50 mL group to the 100 mL group? Think “whole = ___” first.
Steps for Question 5: write “whole = ___” first, then every step.
Which conclusion do the data support?
choices: A) More water always means taller plants.
B) Growth rose up to 100 mL, and 200 mL gave no extra growth.

content.question: Design a new experiment: does the colour of light change how fast lettuce grows? Write: the question, what you change, what you measure, THREE things you keep the same, and how many plants per group.

pomodoros.subject: Social Studies: supply, demand and graphs

content.content:
Practice data (invented for this exercise). A shop in Doha sells bottled water. The table shows how many bottles buyers want (demand) and how many the shop is willing to sell (supply) at each price.
Price per bottle (QAR)1234
Bottles demanded500400300200
Bottles supplied100200300400

A shortage means demand is higher than supply. A surplus means supply is higher than demand. The price where they match is the equilibrium.
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.

content.question: As the price rises, what happens to the number of bottles demanded?
At which price do demand and supply match (equilibrium)?
How big is the SHORTAGE at QAR 1 (bottles demanded minus bottles supplied)?
How big is the SURPLUS at QAR 4 (bottles supplied minus bottles demanded)?
By what percent did the number demanded fall when the price rose from QAR 1 to QAR 2? Give the size of the fall as a positive percent.
Steps for Question 5: write “whole = ___” first, then every step.
In 2 complete sentences: why would a seller lower the price when the shop has a surplus?
What is it called when more is supplied than is demanded?

content.content: Dorothy Vaughan (1910–2008) began work at the Langley laboratory of the NACA in December 1943. She was assigned to the segregated West Area Computing unit, where women did the calculations for wind-tunnel and flight tests by hand. In 1949 she was promoted to lead that group, becoming the NACA’s first Black supervisor. She stayed in that job until 1958, when the NACA became NASA. When electronic computers arrived, she moved to the Analysis and Computation Division and became an expert programmer in the FORTRAN language. She contributed to the Scout launch vehicle program and retired in 1971 after a 28-year career. (Practice passage written for this packet from NASA’s biography of Dorothy J. Vaughan, nasa.gov.)
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.

content.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: A) Dorothy Vaughan led a team, then learned computer programming as the work changed.
B) Computers are faster than people.
D) Dorothy Vaughan liked wind tunnels.

content.question: She began in December 1943 and retired in 1971. How many years was her career?
How many years after she was hired (1943) was she promoted to lead the group (1949)?
What can be inferred from the passage?
choices: A) She stopped learning after her promotion.
B) She kept learning new skills when the work changed.

content.question: What is the author’s main purpose?
choices: A) To entertain with a made-up story
B) To inform readers about a mathematician and her career

pomodoros.subject: Math Part 2: mean, median, range and Fix-It

content.content: Mean = add all, divide by how many. Median = the middle number AFTER you put them in order (with an even count, average the middle two). Range = biggest minus smallest. Re-type the numbers before you calculate.
A runner’s lap times in minutes, in the order she ran them: 15, 9, 19, 12, 15.

content.question: Find the MEAN lap time.
Find the MEDIAN lap time.
Find the RANGE of the lap times.

A price rises from QAR 40 to QAR 50. What is the percent increase? Write “whole = ___” first in your steps.
